#: Built-in preset: Palmetto 800, the South Carolina statewide P25 system.
#preset: Shipped INSIDE the image and selected by the add-on option `preset`. It is not a file you edit -- edits would be lost on update, which is the whole point: fixes to the values below reach you when the add-on updates. Per-install differences go in add-on options instead: `device_overrides` (dongle serial, gain, ppm), `home_assistant`, `audio_output`, and `extra_json` for anything else. To hand-write a full config instead, set `preset: custom` and point `config_file` at it.

devices.name: sdr0
devices.#args: Bare 'rtl' takes the first dongle found, which is right for a single-dongle install. With more than one, set device_overrides[].serial -- the add-on turns that into "rtl=<serial>". init-op25 logs every serial it can see at startup.
devices.#gains: R828D gain steps are discrete (…25.4, 28.0, 29.7, 32.8, 33.8, 36.4, 38.6…) and multi_rx rounds to an int, so 30 lands on 29.7. This was 39 (i.e. 38.6, one step off maximum) through 0.0.7: near-max gain on 800 MHz overloads the tuner into intermodulation, which sounds like a bad decode rather than an overload. Tune it against the symbol quality figure in Tuning & Diagnostics.
devices.#ppm: Set this from device_overrides[].ppm. To measure: let the control channel lock, read 'freq error' (Hz) in Tuning & Diagnostics, divide by 859.2625.
devices.#rate: 2400000 is in multi_rx's approved RTL sample-rate list AND divides exactly by if_rate 24000 (decimation 100), so the arbitrary resampler in p25_demodulator_dev.py is skipped entirely. 1000000 -- used through 0.0.7 -- gave decimation 41 to 24390 Hz and then an arbitrary resample down to 24000. It also widens the tuned window to 2.04 MHz, so fewer voice grants force the dongle to retune (and re-settle its PLL) at the start of a call.

channels.name: Palmetto 800
channels.#destination: One UDP port, consumed by websocket_server for browser audio. Do not add a second destination here to get local speaker output as well -- in the add-on there is no sound device by default. That dual-destination trick is for a standalone install (see apps/Palmetto800-single.json).

chans.#control_channel_list: Richland-area site. The primary is first; the rest are secondaries the site advertises, tried in order during a control-channel hunt. For a different part of the state, replace these with your site's -- everything else in this preset stays valid.
chans.#tgid_tags_file: Resolved relative to work_dir, NOT to this file. Optional: without it you get talkgroup numbers instead of names, which is harmless. radioreference.com is the usual source.
chans.#site: RFSS 2 / Site 32 (0x20); primary CC 859.2625, secondaries per sccb
chans.#crypt_behavior: 2 = do not pass encrypted traffic to audio. Encrypted calls decode to near-silence, so the alternative is recording and transcribing nothing.

#audio: Left empty deliberately: a unicast UDP port has exactly one consumer, and websocket_server needs 23456 to serve /api/stream. The add-on option audio_output overwrites audio.module -- set it to 'alsa' only if the container has been given a sound device.

terminal.#module: terminal.module and terminal_type are forced by the add-on run script (websocket_server.py on ws:0.0.0.0:8099, which is the ingress port). Setting them here would be ignored.

home_assistant.#enabled: Transcription and call recording are off by default. Turn this on and set the add-on option home_assistant.use_supervisor; url and token are injected by the add-on and must not be put here -- /api/config serves this JSON to an unauthenticated browser.
